dimensions.note: No secrets in settings; the Jev key stays in the @swamp/typesafe-ai instance (from a vault) and Capture is reached in process with runModel, so no token is held here. Withheld tasks (text that looks like a token, key, password or email) are never searched for, sent to Jev or logged in Capture (tested; end to end, the withheld task never reached the mock Jev). A heading that looks like a secret is left out of pick questions and request descriptions (tested). logAs is an email by design and is stored in the logged resource only. 2026.11.02.2: the Obsidian Tasks recurrence rule now kept with each task is checked by looksSecret too, and a task whose rule looks like a secret is withheld; the other dropped fields (dates, priority, ids) are never sent anywhere. 2026.11.05.1: candidates holds and reads no secret. It shows only candidates, so a withheld task never appears in its answer (tested).

match logs candidate, found, nothing-found, failed-search and question counts; log logs the outcome counts and warns (logger.warning) when any candidate failed (tested). Task text, queries, extension names, note paths and logAs are never logged. 2026.11.05.1: candidates logs nothing of its own, so no task text reaches the logs; the answer is in its data.

A registry search that exits non-zero, prints non-JSON or throws marks only that task searchFailed. A missing pick, a pick naming an empty slot, runModel missing, a thrown runModel, ok:false from Capture or a result with no request each leave only that task failed, with a reason, and nothing logged (all tested). The pick job is allowFailure per batch and log runs whatever its outcome. Capture errors are cut to 300 characters in the reason. Known edge: a task Capture always rejects (say a description over 20000 characters) stays failed on every run; it is reported, never dropped. 2026.11.02.2: splitTasksFields cannot fail: a task without fields is returned unchanged, and one that is nothing but fields keeps its raw text so it still has a non-empty text (tested). 2026.11.05.1: A stored scan that doesn't parse makes candidates fail rather than say no scan ran (tested), so the router sends the turn to Claude. No stored scan gives a plain answer saying so, distinct from the agreed empty text.

67 tests (8 new in 2026.11.02.2) with a fake registry and a fake Capture, no network: Obsidian Tasks fields in the emoji and Dataview formats, U+FE0F variants, a recurrence rule ending at any field, tasks without fields left byte for byte, a recurring task keeping its id when its date rolls on, the rule in Jev questions and request descriptions, and new stopwords; plus the 2026.11.02.1 coverage of searching, picking, every outcome and AC7 failure path, preview, the stable key and the 90-call cap. End to end against a mock Jev and a scratch Capture: a recurring task logged as request #3, then completed and rolled on a week by hand, stays request #3 with no new request; Jev and Capture never saw its dates; the vault checksum is unchanged. Read-only check on a real 397-task vault: only the 6 recurring tasks change text, each to a clean title with its rule. 2026.11.05.1: 80 tests (13 new in 2026.11.05.1): every outcome's line, one candidate, 23 candidates past the engine's 20-line cap, the empty text from spec version 3, no scan, an unreadable scan, and the recipe's pattern against the spec's phrase compiled as the engine does. Run for real: the recipe through puddlerecipes' recipeFromWorkflow and parseRecipe, and candidates through swamp with no scan and after a preview log. Not yet run: the phrase through the router, which needs the published version in the desk.

Each request carries idempotencyKey obsidian-task-scan:<task id>, the id coming from path and text, so Capture gives back the same request on any rerun (checked end to end). Requests the previous logged run made for the same logAs and captureModel are reused without calling Capture. Capture holds keys per person, so changing logAs logs again for the new person; README and CLAUDE.md say so. A failed search, pick or log is retried on the next run. Overlapping runs could pair a pick with another run's search; the worst case is one run's outcome being wrong for that task, and the next run decides it again. 2026.11.02.2: Obsidian Tasks dates are dropped from the text the id is made from, so a recurring task keeps its id and idempotency key when Obsidian rolls its date on (tested, and end to end). Tasks without fields keep exactly the ids 2026.11.02.1 gave them; a recurring task already logged by 2026.11.02.1 gets a new id once, and so one more request. 2026.11.05.1: candidates writes one fixed-name resource as a new version and changes nothing else. Asking twice gives the same answer until a new scan runs.

Registry: swamp extension search <query> --json, the query passed as one argument (no shell), at most four words of [a-z0-9_-] starting with a letter or digit, so it can never read as a flag; extensions[] rows without a string name are skipped. Capture: create_request with as, title (at most 120 characters), description, candidateExtensions (at most 3) and idempotencyKey (35 characters), all inside Capture's limits; the request id and number are read from the request resource. Pick answers are checked against AnswerSchema. 2026.11.02.2: titles no longer carry Obsidian Tasks dates or emoji fields, and the description adds one line, It recurs <rule>., well within Capture limits. 2026.11.05.1: The recipe is a pack workflow with a puddlerouterRecipe tag and one model_method step, the form @puddleworks/recipes reads; the tag's pattern, dataName and template come from spec version 3's recipe. The extension's new puddlerouter-recipe label makes recipes-sync report no puddlerouterRecipe tag for the scan workflow (puddlerecipes#5), and the recipe still indexes.

Each search is one swamp subprocess with stdin null and piped output, awaited with output() so nothing stays open; at most four at once. No temporary files. At most 90 runModel calls per run, under swamp's limit of 100 per execution; the rest are marked failed and the next run logs them. 2026.11.05.1: candidates opens no file or subprocess, and starts no scan, so it answers inside the router's 15 s limit.

README says the content words of each candidate are sent to the swamp extension registry as a search and that withheld tasks are never sent; examples use you@example.com and someone@example.com. The only address shipped is the default captureUrl, http://127.0.0.1:3002. No personal paths, hostnames or names in shipped files. 2026.11.05.1: Read the changed shipped files: README.md, manifest, obsidian_task_scan.ts and the recipe workflow. Examples are generic. spec/outcome-spec.v3.json has names as the user and emails blank, and isn't shipped.

All new schemas are plain z.object. logAs is empty or a valid email, captureUrl a URL, matchThreshold 0..1. AnswerSchema stays a looseObject on purpose (typesafe-ai answers carry probabilities). request.number is an integer. 2026.11.02.2: Task gains recurrence, optional and non-empty. 2026.11.05.1: CandidatesSchema is a plain z.object with iso datetimes; scannedAt is null only when no scan has run.
result, classified, matched and logged: infinite, keep 20 versions each. 2026.11.05.1: candidates: infinite, keep 20 versions, like the others.
Not a CRUD lifecycle behavior. It creates Capture requests but does not own them: Capture's own methods read, edit and withdraw them.

log decides everything it can before calling Capture: preview, previous reuse, the call cap and runModel being present. Capture itself checks logAs is in its people list and fails the call if not, which leaves the task failed. run still checks folder containment and existence before reading. 2026.11.05.1: candidates reads only its own logged data, and writes only its own answer, so it needs no checks. The extension isn't labelled effects-read because log writes to Capture; the owner names this one method under reads:.
run writes result/result, classify classified/classified, match matched/matched and log logged/logged; one instance each. 2026.11.05.1: candidates writes candidates/candidates; one instance.

log reads the latest logged with readResource, parses it with LoggedSchema and ignores it if it does not parse or cannot be read, so Capture's idempotency key still holds (tested). The pick forEach reads matched.batches with data.latest because forEach.in resolves at job start; every other value is passed as step outputs. 2026.11.05.1: candidates reads the latest logged with readResource and parses it with LoggedSchema; it doesn't read another model's data.

model.version stays 2026.11.02.1: 2026.11.02.2 adds no setting, and the only change to stored shapes is the optional recurrence on each task, which no method needs from an old resource. 2026.11.02.1 moved from 2026.10.23.4 with an upgrade entry, since logAs, captureModel, captureUrl and matchThreshold all default (tested). 2026.11.05.1: Model and manifest go to 2026.11.05.1 with one upgrades entry that leaves global arguments alone, pinned by a new test. The new resource needs nothing from old data.
